So Foundation 6 for sites, the sass version, is a royal pain in the butt to install. However, after 3 days of pain I got it working to the point of being able to actually use it. I will outline these steps now. These are the steps I took, on my remote server, the work flow that you use will most likely be different.

  • Basic update of server: 
sudo apt-get dist-upgrade sudo apt-get update sudo apt-get upgrade
  • Basic security, don't do stuff as root. I used the name "admin" for demonstration purposes only, this is a bad choice in a production environment: 
adduser admin sudo usermod -a -G sudo admin
  • Switch to admin: 
sudo su - admin
  • Install Git: 
sudo apt-get install git
  • Install Node Version Manager (NVM): 
curl -o- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/creationix/nvm/v0.29.0/install.sh | bash
  • Install NodeJS with NVM. Node Package Manager (NPM) comes with NodeJS: 
nvm install 5.0
  • We will not be using Ruby for our css preprocessor, instead we will use libsass, which is faster: 
npm install -g node-sass
  • Nearing the end of this ridiculous addition to our work flow now: 
npm install -g foundation-cli bower gulp
  • We can now use Foundation For sites: 
foundation new <projectname> --libsass

As for incorporating this in to a frameworks, when I get that figured out I will post it. Please rip this to shreds if you see an error, I am an amateur at best and do this mostly as a hobby. However, the install for Foundation 6 Sites is really not well documented and needs some love. I am more than happy to update this if a recommendation is worthwhile. If this helps 1 person avoid the rage that was brought about by trying to install this frontend tool then I will sleep a little better at night.
